metric_rationale: The experimental design explicitly pits Take The Best against Tallying on every single trial. Since the validities are strictly descending in feature index, TTB will always choose the option that wins on the first discriminating feature from left to right. Tallying will always choose the opposite option because the design ensures the other option has a higher total number of positive cues. By computing the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the TTB prediction, we will get a value close to 1.0 for data simulated under TTB, and a value close to 0.0 for data simulated under Tallying.

This metric isolates trials where Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) make diametrically opposed predictions. By computing the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic on these specific trials, we expect Tallying-simulated data to yield a value significantly greater than 0.5, whereas TTB-simulated data will yield a value significantly less than 0.5. With half of the experimental trials designed to be opposing, the metric ensures a highly stable estimate per subject.

This metric isolates trials where Tallying predicts a strict tie (both options have an equal number of winning features). On these tie trials, Tallying predicts random guessing (50% choice probability). In contrast, WADD uses the validities to break the tie, consistently favoring the option with higher-validity features. The metric calculates the proportion of choices on these tie trials that align with the WADD prediction. Tallying should yield a value around 0.5, while WADD will yield a value significantly greater than 0.5.

This metric isolates trials where Tallying predicts a tie (equal number of positive features for both options) but WADD predicts a strong preference for the option with the highest validity feature (feature index 0). Specifically, it looks at Trial 1 (1 vs 1 feature) and Trial 6 (2 vs 2 features). For Tallying, the choice probability for the option with feature 1 is exactly 0.5, regardless of beta or epsilon. For WADD, the option with feature 1 always has a higher weighted sum for any gamma > 0, so the choice probability will be significantly > 0.5. This creates a large and stable mean difference between the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that violate both TTB and Tallying on the critical 'Dominance Violation' trials. On these trials, one option wins on the single highest-validity cue AND has a greater total number of winning cues. The Strategy Mixture model, which probabilistically chooses between TTB and Tallying, strongly predicts this dominant option. However, the WADD model with a gamma > 1 can predict the opposite option, because the second and third highest validities combined can outweigh the single highest validity plus several weak validities. The metric returns the proportion of these WADD-specific choices, which will be near zero for the Mixture model but substantially higher for the WADD model.

This metric evaluates the change in the probability of choosing Option A at the extremes of the feature count differences. Under WADD, the probability of choosing A strictly and monotonically increases as the weighted sum difference shifts in favor of A, predicting a positive difference for both (T2 - T1) and (T10 - T9). Under the Strategy Mixture Theory, because Tallying operates on raw count differences, Tallying strongly favors B in both T1 and T2, and strongly favors A in both T9 and T10. This determinism causes the choice probabilities to plateau at the tails, resulting in a metric value close to zero.

This metric isolates 'Double Agreement' trials where both TTB and Tallying strongly favor the same option, but WADD strongly favors the opposite option due to high-validity compensatory cues. Under the Tallying/TTB mixture theory, since both heuristics agree, the choice probability for this option will be extremely high. Under the WADD/TTB mixture theory, WADD pushes the decision in the opposite direction, significantly lowering the selection rate of the TTB/Tallying favored option.

The experimental design consists of three pairs of trials. In each pair, the predictions of Tallying (count difference) and Take-The-Best (lexicographic winner) are held completely constant, but the Weighted Additive (WADD) score difference shifts from favoring Option B (or a tie) to favoring Option A. This metric calculates the difference in the rate of choosing Option A between the trials where WADD favors A (WADD difference > 0.1) and the trials where WADD favors B or ties (WADD difference < 0.1). Under the Tallying + TTB theory, since the inputs to both heuristics are identical across the sets, the expected metric is exactly 0. Under the WADD + TTB theory, the metric will be strongly positive because the compensatory WADD strategy pulls choices toward Option A in the first set and toward Option B in the second.
